title: SF894 (2021-2022 Regular): Criminal background checks for firearms transfer requirement; grounds for disqualification of transferee permit modification

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2021-02-10; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/92/2021/0/SF/894/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced 2021-02-10. Strikes the old rule that only a prohibition under 624.713 could be a ground to refuse a transferee permit or transfer, the old 'seven-day' waiting-period words, the transferee-permit and transfer-to-unknown-party subdivisions of 624.7132, and extends some delivery rules from pistols and assault weapons to 'firearm'. Section 3 has more exclusions (family, dealers, law enforcement, temporary range or hunting loans) not quoted here. Paragraph (b) of 624.7131 subd. 4 quoted as two sentences joined.

operative_text:
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 2): A person who is not a firearms dealer is prohibited from transferring possession or ownership of a pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon to any other person who is not a firearms dealer, unless the transferee presents a valid transferee permit issued under section 624.7131 and a current state or federally issued identification.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 3), paragraph (d): (d) Both the transferor and the transferee must retain a copy of the record of transfer and any attachments to the record of transfer for 20 years from the date of the transfer.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 4), paragraph (b): (b) A person who refuses or is unable to produce a record of transfer for a firearm transferred under this section in response to a request for production made by a peace officer pursuant to paragraph (a) is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 4), paragraph (b): (b) A chief of police or sheriff shall refuse to grant a permit to a person who is a danger to self or others. The decision of the chief of police or sheriff must be based on documented past contact with law enforcement.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7132, subd. 5), paragraph (b): (b) A chief of police or sheriff shall deny an application if the person is a danger to self or others.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7132, subd. 4): Except as otherwise provided in subdivision 7 or 8, no person shall deliver a pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon to a proposed transferee until five business days after the date the agreement to transfer is delivered to a chief of police or sheriff in accordance with subdivision 1 unless the chief of police or sheriff waives all or a portion of the waiting period.
